Tyson Foerster has one of the heaviest shots in the league (96th percentile by NHL EDGE) and he's using it: 37 shots and 4.3 expected goals in 17 games. He has three goals. That 8.1 percent shooting is well below his usual range, and for a player who scored 61 goals in his first 195 games, it should turn.

The bigger issue is the line around him. Philadelphia gets only 41 percent of the expected goals at 5v5 when he's on, and his teammates' shooting has been kind (2.89 goals above expected), so his five points might be a bit flattering in that sense.

Last season he played only 29 games, so he's still finding his rhythm over a full year. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 31 percent of his entries, a dump-and-chase style that relies on linemates winning races. Our range projects about 22 goals. A finisher on a bad possession line is a bet on the finishing.
headline: Foerster's shot is fine; the goals aren't there
